collections.title: dbt performance and maintainability

collections.description: Recipes that can execute against local DuckDB.
collections.title: DuckDB

collections.description: Recipes for data engineers working with finance-domain data and controls.
collections.title: Finance data engineering

collections.description: Logistics and fleet analytics Recipes, including reusable modelling patterns with relevant operational triggers and domain-specific fleet and shift outcomes.
collections.title: Logistics and fleet analytics

collections.description: Recipes that can execute against Microsoft Fabric Lakehouse, Fabric Warehouse, or both.
collections.title: Microsoft Fabric

collections.description: Recipes for building analytical models with explicit grain, populations, relationships, history, operational time and business rules.
collections.title: Build models that answer the right questions

collections.description: Recipes that can execute against MotherDuck.
collections.title: MotherDuck

recipes.description: Build a dlt pipeline that lands a SaaS or REST API into bronze incrementally under an approved cursor, enforces an approved schema contract for new fields and changed types, keeps refused records visible, and accounts for each load's records by outcome and by extraction, completely where the API offers an independent, enumerable view of what it holds.
recipes.pitch: Land an API into bronze incrementally, with a schema contract for changed fields and an account of every record it can see.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dlt support and are unassessed.
Needs a per-record cursor on each resource, such as an update or creation time; a resource without one is out of scope.
Studio's rest_api connector is a stub; the API needs another dlt route.
recipes.title: Land a SaaS or REST API into bronze with an incremental cursor and a schema contract
trigger: An API source has to load into bronze incrementally instead of reloading everything on every run.
A pipeline breaks whenever the source API adds a field or changes a field's type.
The team has to know which of an API's records landed in bronze, which were refused and why, and which it can show were missed.

recipes.description: Apply a corrected rule to one approved date range of an incrementally loaded model and carry its effect through everything built from it, prove the range matches the new rule and nothing moved except by that effect, and keep normal loads working afterwards.
recipes.pitch: Restate one date range after a logic change, and prove nothing else moved because of it.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
Converting a model to incremental for routine runs belongs to the dbt-full-refresh-to-incremental Recipe.
recipes.title: Backfill a bounded date range after a logic change without a full refresh
trigger: A business rule in an incremental model was corrected, and only a known date range of published history should be restated.
A full refresh would take too long, or would restate history that must stay as first published.
A normal incremental run only loads new data, so it cannot reprocess a date range already loaded.

recipes.description: Build an agreed event-grain fact with an evidence-backed identity rule, deterministic duplicate and correction handling, source lineage, explicit exceptions, and reconciled event counts and additive amounts.
recipes.pitch: Count business events with a defensible identity rule and an audit trail for every source row.
recipes.title: Build a business-event fact with auditable duplicate handling
trigger: Transaction feeds overlap, and source deliveries may be counted as separate business events.
Replayed deliveries change a report's unique event count or additive totals.
A trip or consignment fact must preserve valid similar events and explain conflicting records.

recipes.description: Build a dlt pipeline that lands a set of database tables into bronze, each loaded under its own approved strategy, with deletes and schema changes handled as approved, every run safe to repeat even after a part-way failure, and a table-by-table reconciliation of each approved run over the approved scope in which every difference found has an allowed cause.
recipes.pitch: Land a database's tables into bronze, each the way it changes, and reconcile each approved run against the source with a cause for every difference found.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dlt support and are unassessed.
Studio's source setup cannot register a sql_database connection; it is declared with approval.
Replacing an existing managed connector belongs to managed-connector-to-dlt.
Log-based CDC replication is out of scope; each run reads the source tables.
Without direct database access, loading exported files belongs to file-drop-to-bronze.
Needs read access to the source database, a key per merged table, and a change signal per incremental table.
recipes.title: Load a database table set into bronze with a bounded incremental strategy and landed-data proof
trigger: An operational database's tables have to land in bronze, and reloading every table in full on each run is too slow or too heavy on the source.
The tables change in different ways (rows updated in place, append-only events, small reference tables, deleted rows), so one load strategy does not fit them all.
Downstream teams need a table-by-table reconciliation of what landed in bronze against the source database before they build on it.

recipes.description: Convert an existing full-refresh dbt model to incremental with a strategy chosen from source behaviour and the approved requirements, prove that consumers still see what a full refresh would show under the approved contract, and record the run time before and after.
recipes.pitch: Make a slow full-refresh dbt model incremental, prove its output still matches, and measure the runtime change.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
Downstream incremental models may still miss late, changed or deleted rows; fixing them is separate work.
Structural refactors with no materialization change belong to the dbt-refactor-output-identical Recipe.
recipes.title: Convert a full-refresh dbt model to incremental and show the runtime delta
trigger: A dbt model is correct but a full refresh is too slow or too expensive to run routinely, and gets slower as history grows.
The nightly build is past its window, and one full-refresh model accounts for most of it.
A full-refresh model needs to become incremental without changing what its consumers see.

recipes.description: Restructure existing dbt models so that, within an approved scope, repeated logic has one owner and long models read as named steps, with evidence that every relation a consumer reads keeps its approved contract against a baseline of the unchanged code.
recipes.pitch: Clean up tangled dbt models and prove that nothing your consumers read has changed.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
recipes.title: Refactor dbt models without changing consumer output
trigger: A model has grown into one long query with logic packed inline, and nobody dares change it because dashboards and reports depend on its output.
The same join, lookup or derived key is written again and again across models, and the copies are starting to drift apart.
A mart reads a raw or source table directly instead of going through a staging model.
Reviewers need evidence that what consumers see is identical before and after a structural change.

recipes.description: Record dimension changes with dbt snapshots and build a bounded historical consumer that selects the agreed version for each fact, with controlled changes, boundary tests and reconciliation.
recipes.pitch: Preserve recorded dimension changes and prove that historical events select the right version.
qualifiers: Complete snapshot outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
Records available changes; present-state snapshots cannot reconstruct unobserved history.
recipes.title: Add dimension history with verified historical fact classification
trigger: Customer, asset or vendor attributes change, but past events need a defensible historical classification.
Reports join facts to today's dimension row and silently restate earlier results after master data changes.
A vehicle, driver or delivery zone changes classification and logistics reporting must select the version valid for each event.

recipes.description: Build an event calculation model that selects applicable dated rules, calculates expected amounts and exposes missing or ambiguous matches under approved precedence and correction policies.
recipes.pitch: Calculate historical amounts from the rules that apply to each event, with visible exceptions and independent amount checks.
recipes.title: Build historical event amounts from effective-dated business rules
trigger: Historical fees or surcharges change when a current rate is applied to past events.
Fleet tariffs or fare components vary by resource, customer or service date and need traceable historical calculations.
Overlapping rate versions or retroactive corrections make historical amounts ambiguous.

recipes.description: Build event-to-resource relationships with source provenance, approved cardinality and temporal rules, visible unresolved cases, and count and amount reconciliation for observed assignments or approved allocations.
recipes.pitch: Explain who or what is responsible for each event, with evidence and totals that survive attribution joins.
recipes.title: Build auditable event-to-resource attribution
trigger: Revenue or productivity must be reported by employee, asset or team, but responsibility for each event is unclear.
Joining events to resource assignments duplicates amounts or assigns events outside the relationship's valid time.
Trip or delivery reporting needs defensible driver, vehicle or garage attribution, including shared responsibility.

recipes.description: Author a Fabric Data Pipeline and its schedule as committed code that runs the approved loads, the dbt build and a downstream refresh in order under approved failure, retry and overlap rules, prove its order and failure paths against the committed definition, and run it where an ephemeral Fabric run is approved.
recipes.pitch: Turn a clicked-together Fabric pipeline into committed code whose order, failure rules and schedule are proven against its definition.
qualifiers: Not yet assessed end to end on fabric_lakehouse or fabric_warehouse.
Sequences existing loads and dbt models; it authors only the pipeline, its schedule and the items that invoke them.
Outside a Fabric Domain only the committed definition can be proven; running it needs a Fabric workspace.
Needs a Studio route for dlt to read source files; cloud buckets (ADLS, S3) have none today.
Scheduling on MotherDuck belongs to motherduck-flight-scheduling.
recipes.title: Author a Fabric Data Pipeline that sequences ingestion, dbt, and downstream refresh as committed code
trigger: The nightly loads, the dbt build and the report refresh are run by hand or live only as a pipeline clicked together in the workspace.
Nobody can say what happens to the dbt build and the report refresh when one load fails, times out or is retried.
Production runs on Fabric, and the sequence, its retries and its schedule have to be reviewed and deployed from the repository.

recipes.description: Author a Fabric Direct Lake semantic model as code over the governed gold tables, make the gold layer fit for it, define each approved KPI once as a measure, and prove its tables and relationships on the data it reads and in the platform's model parser, with each measure's expected values computed independently over gold and checked against the deployed model where deploying it is approved.
recipes.pitch: Author one Direct Lake model as code over governed gold, each approved KPI defined once with independently computed expected values.
qualifiers: Not yet assessed end to end on fabric_lakehouse or fabric_warehouse.
Needs the gold layer in a Fabric lakehouse or warehouse that Direct Lake can read through OneLake.
Studio authors the model offline; deploying it and running its acceptance queries need a Fabric workspace.
Proving the model loads needs the platform's semantic-model parser; Studio's managed runtime does not include it today.
A MetricFlow semantic model of the same metrics belongs to metricflow-semantic-model.
Reports and security roles are outside this Recipe.
recipes.title: Author a Direct Lake semantic model as code over governed gold tables
trigger: The gold marts exist and the Power BI team is about to rebuild the star schema by hand in every report.
Report authors import copies of the gold tables into each report, so data lags and each report redefines the same KPI in its own DAX.
A Direct Lake model built straight on the gold tables shows blank members, missing dates or totals that disagree with the gold layer.

recipes.description: Build a dlt pipeline that lands a recurring file drop into bronze so a rerun over an unchanged drop duplicates no delivery's records, reports a delivery complete only when it passes the approved completeness and layout checks, keeps what fails visible with its reason, recovers a part-way failure without loss or duplication, and reports the status of every expected delivery after each run.
recipes.pitch: Land a recurring file drop into bronze so a rerun duplicates nothing, with completeness checks, a schema contract and a status for each expected delivery.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dlt support and are unassessed.
Needs a Studio route for dlt to read the drop; cloud buckets (ADLS, S3) have none today.
Needs each delivery to state its own completeness, such as a control file.
Covers delimited text files such as CSV; JSON, Parquet and Excel are out of scope.
Reading an API or a database belongs to api-to-bronze-incremental-contract or database-tables-to-bronze.
A hand-maintained sheet re-exported whole belongs to governed-spreadsheet-table.
recipes.title: Load a recurring file drop into bronze with file-completeness and schema controls
trigger: A partner or vendor drops files into a folder on a schedule, and bronze has to pick up each delivery without a rerun loading it twice.
Files arrive late, twice, empty, cut short or with a changed layout, and nobody finds out until a report is wrong.
Downstream teams need to know, for every delivery the team expected, whether it arrived complete before they build on it.

recipes.description: For each approved as-of date, list every in-scope supplier bill open then with its open amount, days past due, aging bucket and hold status, total it at the approved grain and reconcile the total to the previous date through its movements, keeping every unprocessable record visible so no amount is lost, counted twice or settled early.
recipes.pitch: Rebuild aged payables and a reconciling roll-forward for any approved as-of date from dated supplier bills, credits, payments and applications.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Settling as of a past date needs dated applications, or an approved rule linking payments and credits to bills.
Reproducing results as known on a past date needs entry timestamps or kept snapshots of the results.
Stops at aging and its roll-forward; duplicate detection, payment runs and ledger tie-out are separate.
recipes.title: Age payables from open items as of any chosen date and reconcile the total
trigger: Finance needs the aged payables for a past month or quarter end, but the payables system only shows what is owed today.
The payables aging is rebuilt by hand in a spreadsheet each month, and its total never ties back to what was billed and paid since the last close.
Treasury or an auditor asks what was owed to which supplier at a past date, how overdue it was and how much was on hold.

recipes.description: For each approved as-of date, list every in-scope receivable open on that date with its open amount, days past due and aging bucket, total it at the approved grain, and compute DSO under the user's approved rules, while every record that cannot be processed stays visible, as an exception or in an explicit run failure, so no amount is lost, counted twice or settled early.
recipes.pitch: Rebuild aged receivables and DSO for each approved as-of date from dated receivable documents, payments and, where recorded, cash applications.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Settling as of a past date needs dated cash applications, or an approved rule linking payments to documents.
Reproducing results as known on a past date needs entry timestamps or kept snapshots of the results.
Stops at aging and DSO; collections, disputes and bad-debt provisioning are separate outcomes.
recipes.title: Age receivables and compute DSO from open invoices as of any chosen date
trigger: Finance needs the aged receivables report and DSO for a past month or quarter end, but the receivables system only shows what is open today.
The aging report and DSO are rebuilt by hand in a spreadsheet each month, and their totals never quite agree with the open invoices.
An auditor asks what was open at a past date and how overdue it was, and someone has to rebuild the answer by hand.

recipes.description: For each period the approved rules compare, set GL actuals beside the approved budget and the selected forecast per cost center and budgeted account, with variance, percentage and large-variance flags, rolled up the approved hierarchy and year to date, while every GL and plan line that cannot be placed stays visible with its reason, so no amount is lost, double counted or read as a real zero.
recipes.pitch: Compare GL actuals with the approved budget and selected forecast per cost center, account and period, with flagged variances and every line reconciled.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Budget and forecast arrive as landed tables; landing and governing the budget spreadsheet is a separate outcome.
A past report as issued needs kept snapshots; without them a later posting into a closed period restates it.
Stops at the comparison; allocations, driver-based planning and plan write-back are separate outcomes.
recipes.title: Compare budget and forecast to actuals at cost-center grain
trigger: Budget-versus-actual is a monthly copy-paste from the general ledger into the budget spreadsheet, and the variances change depending on who built them.
Finance needs each cost center's variance against both the approved budget and the current forecast, with the large ones flagged, before the monthly review.
Department heads dispute their variances because the GL accounts and cost centers do not line up with the lines they budgeted.

recipes.description: Compare in-scope supplier invoices under the user's approved matching rules, list every candidate duplicate pair with the rules that matched, list every invoice once with whether it is a candidate and whether it is held for review and why, and keep every record that cannot be checked visible, as an exception or in an explicit run failure, so no invoice is lost, counted twice or silently cleared.
recipes.pitch: Catch suspected duplicate supplier invoices before they are paid, with the rule behind every match and a hold list the team can act on.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Produces a candidate and hold list; it does not block, release or post anything in the payables or payment system.
Stops at duplicate candidates; purchase order matching, recovering paid duplicates and supplier clean-up are separate.
Results as known on a past date need entry timestamps or kept snapshots of the results.
Past hold lists are not kept; a rule or list change restates every result.
recipes.title: Detect duplicate invoice candidates from explicit matching rules before payment
trigger: Accounts payable paid the same supplier invoice twice and only found out when the supplier returned the money.
Before each payment run, accounts payable wants the suspected duplicate invoices to hold for review, with the rule that flagged each one.
The payables system only catches an exact repeat of the invoice number, so re-keyed numbers and invoices entered under a second supplier record slip through.

recipes.description: At the approved reconciliation grain, including legal entity and currency where relevant, set the general-ledger balance beside its subledger balance, explain the difference as breaks classed under approved rules, leave any residual visible as unexplained, and keep unprocessable records visible as exceptions, so no amount is lost, counted twice or absorbed.
recipes.pitch: Reconcile every control account to its subledger with each break classified and nothing quietly absorbed.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Linking breaks to documents needs a document reference on ledger lines or an approved matching rule.
Reproducing a past tie-out after rule or source changes needs kept history of the tie-out.
Stops at the classified tie-out; correcting postings, sign-off and close packs are separate outcomes.
recipes.title: Tie the general ledger to its subledgers and classify every break
trigger: Month-end close stalls because control accounts do not agree with their subledgers and the difference is worked out by hand in a spreadsheet.
The controller will not sign off until every control-account difference is explained, from late postings to manual journals, with nothing left unexplained.
An auditor asks why a control account differed from its subledger at a past period end, and someone has to rebuild the explanation by hand.

recipes.description: Schedule each contract line's allocated price by period under the approved recognition rules, net billing against it into deferred revenue or the approved asset or receivable at the approved netting level, roll the positions forward at the approved grain, and keep every unprocessable contract or billing line visible, so no amount is lost, counted twice or recognised early.
recipes.pitch: Turn contracts and invoices into a revenue schedule and a deferred-revenue roll-forward that tie to each other and to every invoice line.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Needs contract lines carrying their allocated price and dated terms; price allocation is a separate outcome.
Treats each contract line as one performance obligation; combining lines into one obligation is a separate outcome.
On business dates alone, a backdated change restates earlier periods; reproducing them needs kept history.
Stops at the schedule and roll-forward; journal postings, period locking and translation are separate.
recipes.title: Generate the revenue-recognition schedule and deferred-revenue roll-forward from contracts
trigger: Revenue is spread across months by hand in a spreadsheet and never agrees with the deferred revenue balance or with what was invoiced.
Every month-end someone rebuilds the deferred revenue roll-forward and cannot explain its movement contract by contract.
An auditor asks how much of a contract was recognised in each period and why, including after it was upsold, repriced or cancelled part way through.

recipes.description: Build the trial balance by account and fiscal period, plus entity and currency where more than one is in scope, with opening, debits, credits and closing, roll it up to statement lines, list late postings and invalid journals, and record each period's state at or after its hard close so any later change to it is handled as the approved lock policy says.
recipes.pitch: Rebuild the trial balance and close pack every period, with closed periods recorded, later changes caught and every journal accounted for.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Detecting a change to a closed period needs state that later builds and full refreshes do not rewrite.
Naming a changed line needs stable line ids; lateness and an as-at-hard-close record need posting instants and history.
Stops at the close pack; subledger tie-out, consolidation, FX and posting corrections are separate outcomes.
recipes.title: Produce the trial balance and close pack as code
trigger: The close pack is rebuilt by hand every period and last quarter's trial balance cannot be reproduced as it was when the period closed.
Auditors ask what a closed period showed at its hard close and whether anything was posted into it afterwards.
Controllers need the journals posted after the soft close listed, and a hard stop when a closed period changes.

recipes.description: Build a dlt pipeline and a governed table that load each new export of a hand-maintained spreadsheet under an approved structure contract, keep the last accepted version live when an export breaks it, set aside bad rows with reasons, retain accepted versions as approved, and document every column with its owner.
recipes.pitch: Turn the spreadsheet everyone depends on into a governed table that fails loudly when its structure breaks.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dlt support and are unassessed.
A recurring feed of delivered files that state their own completeness is file-drop-to-bronze.
Each export must be a full copy of the sheet; a partial extract or change feed is out of scope.
Covers a delimited text export such as CSV; reading a workbook directly is out of scope.
Sized for spreadsheet-scale files, not large extracts.
Needs a Studio route for dlt to read the file; cloud buckets (ADLS, S3) have none today.
recipes.title: Promote a spreadsheet or CSV to a governed, tested table
trigger: A spreadsheet that reports and models depend on is edited by hand, and a moved, renamed or retyped column keeps breaking them quietly.
Nobody can say what each column of a hand-maintained file means, who owns it or which row is the key.
A team keeps editing a sheet and re-exporting it, and wants a warehouse table of it that is checked on every new export.

recipes.description: Resolve customer records from several source systems into one golden record per customer, with a two-way crosswalk, approved match and survivorship rules held as data, golden ids that stay stable across runs, an unresolved list that accounts for every source record, and an optional comparison with a source system's own merge pointers.
recipes.pitch: One customer, one stable id, every source record traced to it and every unresolved one explained.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
Expects names and addresses already standardized, with a match key, by an earlier standardization step.
Stable golden ids need the id register to persist between runs; a rebuild from scratch reissues them.
Without retained crosswalk history, the crosswalk as it stood on a past run cannot be reconstructed.
recipes.title: Deduplicate customers into a golden record with a source crosswalk
trigger: The same customer exists in several systems under different ids, so customer counts and per-customer revenue are inflated.
Analysts need to trace a golden customer to every source record behind it, and any source record to its golden customer.
Source systems disagree on a customer's name, address or contact details and nobody can say which value wins or why.
Customer ids change from one run to the next when a later record turns out to belong to an existing customer.

recipes.description: Standardize every source record's name and postal address under approved, editable rules, keep the original values beside the standardized ones, mint deterministic match keys that agree exactly when the standardized values agree, and account for every record as standardized or excluded with a reason, without merging records.
recipes.pitch: Give every customer record a clean name, a clean address and a match key you can explain.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
Addresses are standardized by rule, not verified against a postal service, so deliverability is not checked.
recipes.title: Standardize names and addresses and mint deterministic match keys
trigger: The same customer is written differently across CRM, billing and support, so joins on name or address miss.
A deduplication or golden-record step needs stable, explainable match keys before any fuzzy matching.
Addresses arrive in mixed formats across countries, so reports group the same address several ways.
Match results must be reproducible from run to run, without depending on run order or an external service.

recipes.description: Author a new incremental dbt model with an enforced output contract, then prove that a rerun and a re-delivery of records already applied leave it unchanged under the approved definition, with records the approved rules set aside kept visible.
recipes.pitch: Build an incremental dbt model with an enforced contract and show that a rerun or a re-delivery of records already applied leaves it unchanged.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Needs a source that carries a key and a version or update timestamp for each record, and can be read in full.
Converting an existing full-refresh model belongs to the dbt-full-refresh-to-incremental Recipe.
recipes.title: Author an incremental dbt model with its contract and prove idempotency
trigger: A new dbt model must be brought up to date incrementally on each run, and nobody can show that a rerun or a re-delivery of records already applied leaves it unchanged.
Downstream consumers need a guaranteed set of columns, types and keys, and a build should fail when the output drifts from them.
A loader resends or corrects records, and the table must stay correct when the same batch is delivered twice.

recipes.description: Bring a legacy SQL script or view into dbt as models that publish the same contract, proven against the legacy logic's own output on the same inputs, with legacy defects reproduced and reported as follow-up work.
recipes.pitch: Retire a hand-run SQL script by rebuilding it in dbt and proving the new models return exactly what the old one did.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
Needs the legacy output on the same inputs, from the legacy SQL or its current table.
recipes.title: Convert a legacy SQL script or view into a dbt model and prove parity
trigger: A report or table is still produced by a hand-run SQL script or a database view outside dbt, with no tests, lineage or review.
The team wants to retire a legacy script, but its consumers need proof that the dbt version returns exactly the same rows.
Transformation logic written as step-by-step SQL (temp tables, updates, deletes) has to move into the dbt project.

recipes.description: Build fleet utilisation with authoritative asset availability, maintenance-adjusted time, separate observation coverage and traceable numerator and denominator components that reconcile across daily and monthly reporting.
recipes.pitch: Measure fleet use against defensible available asset time while keeping missing observations and maintenance evidence visible.
recipes.title: Build fleet utilisation against explicit asset availability
trigger: A fleet dashboard labels observed vehicle occupancy as utilisation without an authoritative available-time denominator.
Fleet capacity reports omit available vehicles that never come online or subtract overlapping maintenance twice.
Daily and monthly vehicle utilisation disagree because roster, observation and downtime windows differ.

recipes.description: Replace a managed connector with an owned dlt pipeline landed side by side with the connector's tables, reconciled table by table over parallel runs with a cause for every difference, and stopped short of cutover.
recipes.pitch: Swap a Fivetran or Airbyte connector for a dlt pipeline you own, and prove table by table that it lands what the connector did before you cut over.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
Needs read access to the connector's landed tables and to the source the connector reads.
Database sources need a dlt route Studio supports; its sql_database route is not supported today.
recipes.title: Replace a Fivetran or Airbyte connector with a dlt pipeline and reconcile the result
trigger: A managed connector's bill changed shape, or it broke and the vendor fix has been pending for weeks, and the team wants the load in code it owns.
dbt models read a Fivetran or Airbyte connector's tables, so a replacement has to keep landing data those models can use.
Before switching off a managed connector, the team needs proof that its replacement lands the same records, with a reason for every difference.

recipes.description: Resolve accounts to their parent and ultimate parent under approved precedence and parent rules, keep accounts the rules cannot place explicitly unresolved unless an approved fallback places them, roll measures up every level of each corporate family for the approved periods, and list every hierarchy anomaly with its reason, never double counting an account or inventing hierarchy.
recipes.pitch: See every corporate family's total, with every account placed or explicitly unresolved and every broken parent link explained.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
Families as they stood in past periods need dated parent-link history; without it they cannot be rebuilt.
Accounts must already be one record per company; this Recipe does not deduplicate accounts.
recipes.title: Resolve B2B account hierarchies and roll measures to the ultimate parent
trigger: Sales and finance cannot see total revenue or pipeline for a whole corporate family because subsidiaries sit as separate accounts.
The CRM's parent-account field has gaps, loops and conflicts with a firmographic vendor, and nobody knows which link to trust.
After an acquisition or divestiture, reports disagree on which family a past month's revenue belongs to.
Named-account or territory rules apply at the ultimate-parent level and need each account mapped to its parent and ultimate parent.

recipes.description: Bring a materialized view into dbt as a model that publishes the same contract and computes each refresh under the same approved rule, proven against the view's own output after each compared refresh, with view defects reproduced and reported as follow-up work.
recipes.pitch: Retire a materialized view by rebuilding it in dbt and proving each compared refresh matches the view's.
qualifiers: Not yet assessed end to end on fabric_lakehouse or redshift.
Needs the view's definition (Studio can't yet read it on these targets), refresh rule and output at refresh points.
recipes.title: Convert a materialized view into a dbt model and preserve its required refresh semantics
trigger: Warehouse logic lives in a materialized view that nobody can test, review or trace, and the team wants it in the dbt project.
Consumers depend on what each refresh of the view produces, so the dbt model must keep what every refresh computes, not only its final rows.
The view's refresh is opaque, and the team wants its refresh rule stated and owned in code before the view is retired.

recipes.description: Implement a metric with approved eligibility, numerator and denominator components, missing-value and zero-denominator policies, weighting, dimension coverage and verified rollups at supported grains.
recipes.pitch: Make the metric's population and components explicit so its values and supported totals can be checked.
recipes.title: Build a metric with explicit eligibility and reconcilable rollups
trigger: A new percentage, rate or average needs a defensible eligible population and missing-value policy.
Daily and monthly metrics disagree, or totals change when a report groups the same records differently.
Trip tips, vehicle occupancy or delivery service rates depend on eligibility, measurement coverage and weighting.

recipes.description: Define the approved metrics once as dbt MetricFlow semantic models over a gold fact mart, prove that the values the semantic layer returns equal an independent computation of each approved definition at the approved precision, and reconcile them to the agreed reference figures, every difference named and sized; code only, nothing published.
recipes.pitch: Define each metric once, prove its numbers, and name and size every difference from the agreed reference figures.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; motherduck and redshift rely on MetricFlow support and are unassessed.
Needs MetricFlow installed where metrics are queried; Studio's managed runtime does not include it today.
Needs a gold fact mart with a declared grain; changing existing marts or building new fact marts is outside this Recipe.
Code only; publishing to a semantic-layer service or BI tool is outside this Recipe.
recipes.title: Define governed metrics as a MetricFlow semantic model over a gold mart
trigger: Revenue or average order value means different things in different marts and dashboards, and nobody can say which number is right.
Each new report re-implements the same KPI in SQL with its own filters, and the copies drift apart.
A rate gives a different answer by day than by month because copies aggregate it differently.
Analysts need agreed metrics they can slice by agreed dimensions and periods without knowing the joins.

recipes.description: Author a MotherDuck Flight as committed code that runs the approved load and then the dbt build of an approved selection on a schedule, under approved failure, recovery and overlap rules, prove its order, failure paths and carried project against the committed program, and run it in a MotherDuck sandbox where approved.
recipes.pitch: Replace the laptop cron with a committed MotherDuck Flight that loads, builds and fails loudly on a schedule.
qualifiers: Not yet assessed end to end on motherduck.
Schedules the load and build on MotherDuck only; local DuckDB has no scheduler.
The dbt project the Flight carries must fit MotherDuck's Flight source-code size limit.
A schedule only runs on a MotherDuck plan that offers scheduled Flight runs.
The load must reach its source from the Flight runtime, with credentials held as Flight secrets.
Scheduling on Fabric belongs to fabric-data-pipeline-as-code.
recipes.title: Schedule a dlt load and a dbt build on MotherDuck as a committed MotherDuck Flight
trigger: The MotherDuck load and the dbt build that follows it run from a cron job on someone's laptop.
A dlt load and a dbt build on MotherDuck have to run in order on a schedule without standing up an orchestrator.
A scheduled run reports success while the load or the build behind it actually failed.

recipes.description: Bring a hand-run notebook transformation into dbt as models that publish the same contract, proven against what the unchanged notebook writes on the same inputs, with its implicit dataframe behaviour and defects reproduced and reported as follow-up work.
recipes.pitch: Retire a hand-run notebook by rebuilding its dataframe logic in dbt and proving the new models publish what the notebook did.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
Needs the notebook's output on the same inputs, from a run of the unchanged notebook or its current table.
recipes.title: Convert a notebook transformation into a dbt model and prove parity
trigger: A table or report is still produced by running a notebook by hand, pulling warehouse data into dataframes, with no tests, lineage or review.
The team wants the notebook's logic in the dbt project, but its consumers need proof that the dbt version returns the same results.
Dataframe code (merges, group-bys, fills, de-duplication, pivots) has to move into dbt models without changing what the notebook published.

recipes.description: Build evidence-backed state and location intervals, split them across agreed reporting boundaries, and reconcile durations with explicit unknown periods, missing closes and source lineage.
recipes.pitch: Explain how long each entity spent in a state and where, without inventing locations or filling unknown time with activity.
recipes.title: Build state durations by entity, location and reporting period
trigger: Waiting, idle, available or busy time must be measured by site or zone and hour from operational event histories.
State and location change independently, leaving reports unable to explain where an entity spent its time.
Vehicle or equipment events have missing closes or observation gaps that could inflate operational duration totals.

recipes.description: For each approved as-of date, judge every in-scope order line on time, in full and both under the user's approved promise, tolerance and partial-shipment rules, give each miss one reason, roll the verdicts up by order, customer, carrier and plant from the lines, and keep every excluded record visible with its reason.
recipes.pitch: One delivery figure per order line, order, customer, carrier and plant, with a reason for every miss and nothing dropped.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Needs order lines (promise date, quantity) and shipment legs (dates, quantities, plus plant and carrier for the cuts).
Stops at delivery verdicts and cuts; freight cost, carrier contracts, forecasting and inventory are separate outcomes.
A past as-of date reproduces only from kept promise and cancellation history; a rebuild restates it.
Order and shipment tables already in the Domain; exported files go to file-drop-to-bronze first.
recipes.title: Measure on-time-in-full delivery by customer, carrier and plant
trigger: Customers report late deliveries, and Sales, Supply Chain and the carriers each quote a different on-time-in-full figure because each applies its own promise date, tolerance and partial-shipment rule.
A late or short order cannot be traced to a plant, a carrier or a customer change, so each side blames another.
A shipment is split across days, carriers or plants, or the customer moved the promise date, and no report says whether the line counted as on time, in full or neither.
Cancelled lines, lines not yet due, undelivered lines and shipments matching no order line fall out of the delivery figure with no stated reason.

recipes.description: Classify every leaver, compute attrition rates for the approved cuts under the user's approved definitions, show how tenure is spread across current staff and how each hire cohort is retained, and reconcile leavers to the headcount roll-forward, while every termination record stays accounted for and small groups stay hidden where the approved policy hides them.
recipes.pitch: One attrition, tenure and retention picture built on the same people the headcount counts, with every leaver accounted for.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Needs per-worker period-end state with population status (and FTE if the base uses it) and its roll-forward.
Needs termination records with a date, a reason code and the worker's placement on the last day worked.
Results as known on a past date need kept snapshots; backdated HR changes restate past periods.
Stops at attrition, tenure and retention; building headcount, pay and forecasting are separate outcomes.
recipes.title: Measure attrition, tenure and hire-cohort retention from the headcount outputs
trigger: Leadership asks whether attrition is rising and where, and nobody can answer from one consistent set of figures.
HR and finance quote different turnover rates for the same year because each counts leavers and headcount differently.
Nobody can say whether recent hires leave faster than earlier ones, or how long people stay before they go.

recipes.description: From effective-dated job history, place every worker in the approved population at each reporting date, publish headcount and FTE at the approved grain with org roll-ups, explain each period's change through approved movement classes, and keep every excluded or unprocessable record visible so no worker is lost or counted twice.
recipes.pitch: Turn effective-dated HR job history into one month-end headcount and FTE everyone can use, with a roll-forward that ties every period.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Past headcount needs effective-dated job history; a current-state worker table cannot show past moves.
Reproducing figures as known on a past date needs entry timestamps or kept snapshots of the results.
Stops at headcount, FTE and the roll-forward; attrition, tenure, payroll and positions are separate.
recipes.title: Build period-end headcount and FTE by org and a roll-forward that ties every period
trigger: HR, finance and the board deck each report a different headcount for the same month-end, and nobody can say why.
Every month someone rebuilds opening plus hires minus leavers plus transfers in a spreadsheet, and it never equals the closing headcount.
Leadership asks how many people a team had at a past month-end, under the org structure that applied then.

recipes.description: For the approved review date, place each counted worker's pay against the band in force, keep that worker-level result apart from the published outputs, and publish only approved aggregates, such as unadjusted pay gaps, with the approved small-group hiding, while every record is accounted for.
recipes.pitch: Check pay against salary bands and publish approved pay gaps by group, with approved small-group hiding and its remaining limits stated.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Pay, band and worker records arrive as landed tables; landing them is a separate outcome.
Stops at the check and the aggregate report; remediation, adjusted-gap modelling and pay planning are separate outcomes.
Restricting worker-level pay needs roles and grants (pii-classification-and-masking); without them it is a label.
On fabric_lakehouse, SQL grants do not govern OneLake reads, so restriction cannot be assured there.
Statutory report formats and statistical significance are separate outcomes.
Hiding small groups alone does not make a figure safe to release; totals and other releases can reveal one.
Unless issued reports are frozen, a later correction restates them; frozen ones need kept snapshots.
recipes.title: Check pay against salary bands and report pay gaps at an aggregate grain
trigger: A pay-equity review is due and worker-level compensation cannot be shared widely.
Managers are told people are paid outside the band, but nobody can say how many, where, or on which band version.
HR is asked for pay gaps between groups and cannot tell whether publishing a number could reveal a small group.

recipes.description: At the approved reconciliation grain, set the payroll register total, mapped to GL accounts, beside what the ledger posted, explain the difference as breaks classed under approved rules, leave any residual visible as unexplained, and account for every register line and ledger posting.
recipes.pitch: Reconcile payroll to the ledger at every cut-off with each break classified and nothing quietly absorbed.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Linking postings to pay runs needs a run reference on the ledger or an approved matching rule.
Needs a pay-code mapping to GL accounts, supplied or agreed; the Recipe never infers one.
Reproducing a past tie-out after rule or source changes needs kept history of the tie-out.
Stops at the classified tie-out; payroll calculation, correcting journals and sign-off are separate outcomes.
Payroll registers keyed by pay run; document-linked control accounts belong to finance-gl-subledger-tieout.
recipes.title: Tie payroll to the general ledger at every cut-off and classify every break
trigger: Payroll expense in the general ledger does not match the payroll register at close, and the gap is worked out by hand.
Finance cannot say which pay run or cost center explains the difference between the register and the ledger.
An auditor asks what an accrual, an off-cycle run or a misposting did to a period, and someone has to rebuild the answer.

recipes.description: Classify every column of the governed relations as a kind of personal data or as not personal, serve a lower-privilege audience each kind masked as approved, limit that audience to the approved access, prove the masked outputs correct whether or not grants are applied, and, where applying the grants is approved, verify each role's effective access, including whether clear values can be recovered.
recipes.pitch: Classify personal data by column, mask it by kind for a lower-privilege audience, and verify that audience's access where grants are applied.
qualifiers: Not yet assessed end to end on fabric_warehouse or redshift.
Needs database roles and per-object grants on the target; DuckDB and MotherDuck have neither.
Applying the roles and grants and running the role checks need a live warehouse and approval to change access.
Fabric Lakehouse is excluded because its SQL endpoint grants do not govern OneLake or Spark reads.
Assumes the lower-privilege audience has no storage-level read path that bypasses database grants.
Finds personal data inside free text only as far as the approved discovery rules reach.
Row-level security, sensitivity labels, encryption, erasure and access auditing are outside this Recipe.
recipes.title: Tag personal-data columns, mask them by kind for a lower-privilege audience and prove the masked outputs
trigger: Analysts need tables that carry names, addresses, emails, phone numbers or ID numbers they must not see.
Nobody can say which published columns hold personal data, so a new column can leak it unnoticed.
An auditor asks to see exactly what a lower-privilege user can read, and whether the clear values can be reached another way.

recipes.description: Produce an independent assessment of an existing dbt change against approved requirements and baselines, with semantic checks, evidence gaps and a merge recommendation while preserving the reviewed implementation.
recipes.pitch: Review the business answers behind a dbt change with independent evidence and leave its implementation unchanged.
recipes.title: Assess an existing dbt change for safe merge without modifying it
trigger: An existing dbt change builds successfully but reviewers still need evidence that its business answers remain valid.
A change to fleet, shipment or financial models needs independent checks against agreed requirements and an approved baseline.
A reviewer must distinguish an implementation defect from missing data, missing relationships or insufficient test coverage.

recipes.description: Author a consumer pipeline as committed code that starts each period's build only when the required upstream feeds meet the approved readiness signal, handles missed, late and restated periods as the approved rules say, and fails explicitly without building when a required feed misses its deadline.
recipes.pitch: Start the build when the data is ready, not when the clock says so, and fail loudly instead of building on partial data.
qualifiers: Needs each required upstream feed to expose an approved readiness signal per period.
Not yet assessed end to end on any listed target.
Needs an orchestrator that can wait for readiness, check it and fail a run.
Studio's orchestration templates do not yet include a readiness gate for every listed target.
Checks readiness by polling within an approved window; event-triggered starts are out of scope.
recipes.title: Gate a consumer pipeline on upstream data readiness instead of a clock
trigger: A consumer build runs at a fixed time and, on runs where an upstream load is late, builds on partial data without anyone noticing.
The schedule was pushed later to be safe, so in an ordinary period the consumers wait hours for no reason.
Several upstream teams land data at different times, and the build must start only when the feeds it needs are ready, and fail loudly when one misses its deadline.

recipes.description: For each approved as-of date, tie every in-scope booking line to what was scheduled, billed after credit memos and collected, split each gap into breaks classed under the user's approved rules, show any residual as unexplained, and keep every unplaceable record visible with its reason.
recipes.pitch: Reconcile what was booked to what was billed and what was collected, with every gap named and nothing quietly absorbed.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Billing needs a stated booking-line reference and cash a stated invoice application, or an approved matching rule.
Stops at the classified tie; revenue recognition, ageing, commission and ledger tie-out are separate outcomes.
Reproducing a past as-of result after back-dated changes needs kept history; a rebuild restates it.
recipes.title: Tie bookings to billings to cash and classify every break
trigger: RevOps and Finance each quote booked, billed and collected, and the three numbers never agree because every team ties them together with its own spreadsheet.
A signed booking is billed late, billed twice or billed after it was cancelled, or an invoice has no booking behind it, and nobody sees it until the customer calls.
Cash arrives that nobody can match to an invoice, or an invoice is part paid, and the gap between billed and collected has no stated reason.

recipes.description: Capture one row per opportunity per user-confirmed snapshot period, such as hourly, daily, weekly or monthly, in an append-only snapshot, then derive stage transitions, conversion rates and close-date slippage with explicit handling of missed periods, reopened and deleted opportunities.
recipes.pitch: Reproduce the pipeline as it stood at each captured snapshot period and measure how deals move, convert and slip.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
History starts at the first snapshot; earlier pipeline cannot be reconstructed from present state.
Capture cannot see changes that happen and revert between two captures; longer periods hide more.
Assessed with a labelled synthetic fixture standing in for the CRM; no live opportunity source was captured.
Assessed at a daily period only; rules for other periods, capture moments, late runs and empty reads are unassessed.
recipes.title: Build a periodic opportunity pipeline snapshot with stage conversion and slippage
trigger: The CRM overwrites opportunity stage, amount and close date, so past pipeline cannot be reproduced as it stood at an earlier point.
RevOps needs stage-to-stage conversion rates by cohort, but only the current opportunity state is available.
Forecast reviews need to know which deals slipped their close date, shrank or grew, and between which snapshots it happened.

recipes.description: Credit each booking to the reps and periods the user's approved plan rules name, flag commission eligibility, roll credit against quota, and keep every booking or quota that cannot be credited visible as an exception.
recipes.pitch: Turn written compensation plan rules into tested, traceable commission-eligible bookings and quota attainment.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
Stops at commission-eligible bookings and attainment; payout amounts are a separate outcome.
Assessed with a labelled synthetic fixture standing in for CRM bookings, rep assignments, quotas and plan rules.
Credit ignoring today's owner needs owner history in the source; the assessed fixture had none.
recipes.title: Build commission-eligible bookings and quota attainment from explicit plan rules
trigger: Reps, managers and finance disagree on attainment because each team credits bookings with its own spreadsheet logic.
Compensation plan rules for eligibility, crediting splits and timing live in documents, not in tested models.
A rep moved territory, a deal was cancelled or a plan changed mid-year, and nobody can say which bookings counted in a closed period.

recipes.description: Bring a scalar warehouse function into the dbt project as a macro, switch the agreed callers to it, and prove that the SQL the macro generates matches the unchanged function and that each switched caller keeps its approved output, with its quirks reproduced and reported as follow-up work.
recipes.pitch: Move a hidden warehouse function into dbt as a macro and prove the SQL it generates gives what the function did.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
Needs the unchanged function runnable on the same inputs, or its outputs captured on them.
Scalar functions only; rewriting a caller's own logic belongs to legacy-sql-to-dbt.
Excludes nondeterministic functions and those whose semantics need side effects, privileges or unreproducible state.
recipes.title: Convert a scalar SQL function into a dbt macro and prove equivalence
trigger: Models or views call a scalar function created directly in the warehouse, so dbt cannot see the dependency and changes to it are not reviewed or tested.
A freshly built environment breaks because the warehouse function its models call does not exist there.
The team wants to retire a warehouse function, but its callers need proof that the SQL the dbt version generates gives the same values.

recipes.description: Build per-ticket response and resolution SLA outcomes from ticket status, priority, team and reply history under approved targets, calendars, pauses, reopens and policy versions, then derive attainment by period, priority and team, a daily open-backlog age view and an exceptions list that accounts for every ticket, with an optional vendor comparison when ticket-level vendor results exist.
recipes.pitch: See how every SLA number is computed and how old the open backlog was on any past day.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
Past backlog needs retained status, priority and team history; without it, backlog starts at the first captured day.
The vendor comparison needs the vendor's per-ticket, per-clock result; without that export it is left out.
recipes.title: Track ticket SLA attainment and backlog aging outside the vendor dashboard
trigger: The ticketing vendor's dashboard reports SLA met or breached, but nobody can check how its numbers are calculated.
Support leads need the open backlog by age as it stood on a past day, which the vendor dashboard cannot show.
SLA attainment must be reported by period, priority and team under the support team's own hours, pauses and reopen rules.
A breach must be traceable to the business hours, pauses and policy version that applied to that ticket.

recipes.description: Build shift-grain revenue, cost and margin components from defensible event assignments and approved cost allocations, with visible cost completeness and reconciled driver, vehicle and period rollups.
recipes.pitch: Explain shift economics with traceable revenue, complete cost status and allocations that conserve source amounts.
recipes.title: Build shift revenue, cost and margin with reconciled rollups
trigger: A fleet dashboard reports revenue per shift but cannot establish whether a shift covers its applicable costs.
Driver performance or vehicle economics need supported trip assignments and shared costs allocated at shift grain.
Shift margins disagree with driver, vehicle or period totals, or low-exposure shifts dominate a ranking.

recipes.description: Give every source table a dbt project declares a freshness limit, or a recorded exemption, and gate the builds that run the check so a source past its fail limit holds back the work the approved failure policy names before it rebuilds, with a report of each table's age, its limit and the work held back.
recipes.pitch: Give every source a freshness limit and stop stale data before downstream models rebuild on it.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Protects only work whose source is judged in the same build; how often builds run is outside this Recipe.
Each checked table needs a measurable load time, such as a landing column, a load log, table metadata or a proxy.
Gating consumer pipelines on upstream readiness belongs to the readiness-gated-orchestration Recipe.
recipes.title: Declare source freshness SLAs and make stale data fail before downstream work
trigger: A load stopped and nothing failed; downstream models rebuilt on old data and the reports still looked current.
Only some sources have a freshness check, often one blanket threshold, and nobody can say which tables are checked or against what.
A stale source must stop the work that depends on it before it rebuilds, and say which source is late, by how much and against what limit.

recipes.description: Convert a Spark ingestion notebook into an owned dlt pipeline that lands beside the notebook's tables, reloads an already-loaded, unchanged file without duplicating, losing or changing a record beyond its load-time and bookkeeping columns, accounts for every source record and every notebook step, and is reconciled table by table with a cause for every difference.
recipes.pitch: Turn a Spark ingestion notebook into a dlt pipeline you own, and prove table by table what it lands and why any row differs.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dlt support and are unassessed.
Needs the notebook's code, the tables it landed, and read access to the files it reads.
Needs a Studio route for dlt to read the notebook's source files; cloud buckets (ADLS, S3) have none today.
recipes.title: Convert a Spark ingestion notebook into a dlt pipeline and reconcile what it lands
trigger: A Spark notebook lands raw files into bronze, and the team wants that load as tested pipeline code without keeping a cluster for it.
An ingestion notebook nobody can change safely mixes parsing, renames and deduplication in cells with no tests, and reruns surprise people.
Models read the tables a Spark notebook lands, so a replacement has to land data they can keep using and account for every difference before anyone switches.

recipes.description: Move a stored procedure that maintains a table run after run into dbt, with each procedural step that shapes the table mapped to a dbt equivalent and parity with the unchanged procedure shown after every compared run, procedure defects reproduced and reported, and retirement only as approved.
recipes.pitch: Retire a stored procedure by rebuilding it in dbt and proving the table matches after every compared run, not only at the end.
qualifiers: Not yet assessed end to end on fabric_warehouse or redshift.
Needs the procedure's table after each compared run, from the unchanged procedure or approved snapshots.
Views and one-shot scripts that rebuild their whole output each run belong to the legacy-sql-to-dbt Recipe.
Procedures that keep row history, such as hand-rolled slowly changing dimensions, are out of scope.
Applies when the maintained table is the required outcome and all relevant behaviour is represented through its state.
recipes.title: Convert a stored procedure into a dbt model and prove parity
trigger: A nightly load is a stored procedure nobody fully understands, and it inserts, updates, deletes or merges rows in a table people depend on.
The team wants the procedure's logic in dbt with tests and lineage, but consumers need proof the table ends up the same after every run.
A procedure that maintains a table in place has to move into the dbt project before it can be retired.
